text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The co-ruling Polish Peasant Party (PSL) wants the Prime Minister to disclose the Interior Ministry report on the recently dismissed Foreign Trade Minister Jacek Buchacz and to apologise for the brusque manner of his dismissal.
- South Korea's LG Group will invest over $700 million in Poland by 2000, the Korean concern's representatives said.
- The Katowice-based tax office received 13 motions from coal companies and mines demanding a coal price increase, but in all cases the office decided to delay its decision.
- Males between 18 and 24 years old and over 50 make up the majority of buyers of mass privatisation NFI units on the primary market, the Privatisation Ministry said.
- Piotrkow Trybunalski based Elpol has started production of horticultural mini-tractors equipped with a 20 horsepower engine. This year's output will reach 230 tractors, Elpol representatives said.

- Poland's food prices fell 0.1 percent in the period from August 10 to August 20 after staying flat in the previous ten days, and were 0.1 percent higher than in the same period in July, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Merrill Lynch investment bank will provide the Gdansk refinery with a $100 million five-year loan as the first tranche of the refinery's $400 million investment programme.
- The listed Budimex construction firm will carry out an $8 million office building construction contract for Norway's Interscandia company, Budimex representatives said.
- California-based Bank of America plans equity investment in Poland that could reach tens of millions of dollars, the bank's Warsaw branch representative said.
- The total number of credit cards issued by Polish banks exceeded 200,000 in August. By year-end 250,000 cards will be issued, the issuing banks say.
- Polifarb Debica paint maker, controlled by National Investment Fund (NFI) 11, will present its share issue prospectus by the end of September this year, NFI 11 representatives said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Poland has only used 0.5 percent of the World Bank's $200 million construction industry loan due to excessive interest rates on credits demanded by Budbank construction bank, the loan's appointed re-distributor, Construction Ministry expert Jerzy Radko said.
- More than 30 companies have already decided to participate in the Second International Cargo Forwarding Fair taking place in Szczecin at the end of October.
- Germany's Henkel chemical concern will sell its Helenowek-based plant to France's L'Oreal cosmetics maker, Henkel Poland representatives said.
- The average salary in the business sector grew by 4.8 percent in August and reached 966.76 zlotys, GUS report said.
ZYCIE WARSZAWY

- Poland's Culture Minister Zdzislaw Podkanski applied to the Patent Office to withdraw the right to use Frederic Chopin's profile to promote vodka, the right to which is currently held by the Siedlce-based Polmos distillery.
- Czech Skoda Liaz truck maker will start assembling Skoda Liaz trucks in the Polish Lancut-based plant co-owned by the Czech Motokov trader, Motokov's deputy director Vaclav Vysin said.

- More than 50 firms are participating in the Infrabud road and bridge construction fair in Katowice, southern Poland. The exhibitors are presenting state-of-the-art projects, construction materials, machines and technology.
- Old age pensioners and full-time employees make up the brunt of Poland's taxpayers, a finance ministry report said.
PARKIET

- The Warsaw Stock Exchange (WSE) has signed an agreement on real-time distribution of the bourse's information data with Dow Jones Telerate. The new service is likely to appear in late September or early October.

- Sobieslaw Zasada Centrum automotive group reported a net loss of 5.2 million zlotys in 1996's first half caused by the need to create reserves demanded by its auditors, Zasada spokesman Franciszek Gaik said.

- Poland's industrial climate improved over August for the second month running, GUS data said. Only the construction industry reported a slight decline but its results were still better than in the same period last year.
